commentary_segments.text: The two-stage current amplifier is shown in this slide. Obviously, a compensation capacitor is now required, which will cause more current to flow in the second stage. The main advantage is however that the output swing can be larger. Also, more gain can be achieved without the use of cascodes. Again, bipolar transistors are used at the input to have a smaller input resistance. Is this why smaller values can be used for the series input resistor R , yielding higher gain-bandwidth combinations? S The input cascode transistors determine the noise performance in single-stage current amplifiers. Active loads are now used for these cascodes. Is their noise still dominant? The answer is positive. Indeed, at higher frequencies, the compensation capacitance acts as a short-circuit. The second stage is little more than an impedance 1/g . This is a low impedance. m2 The noise of the input cascodes is therefore still dominant.
